newsitem.title: USA: Bell Atlantic sees merger closing delayed.
newsitem.headline: Bell Atlantic sees merger closing delayed.

text.p: Bell Atlantic Corp said its merger with NYNEX Corp was being held up by delays in federal regulatory approval and it expected the closing to be delayed past the April 22 date on which it had envisioned closing the deal.
"Obviously things are moving slower than we had hoped," Bell Atlantic spokesman Eric Rabe told Reuters.
"Here we are at March 20 and we still have the (U.S.) Justice Department offering no indication (when they will approve the deal)," Rabe said.

The Bell Atlantic spokesman noted that the U.S. Federal Communications Commission has said it will take 30 days after the Justice Department completes its antitrust review before it gives its final assent to the deal.
Separately, N.Y. State Attorney General Dennis Vacco criticized a decision taken earlier Thursday by New York State utility regulators to approve the Bell Atlantic-NYNEX merger.
He said the conditional blessing granted for the deal by the New York State Public Service Commission (NYPSC) had failed to address the issue of rate relief for consumers.
"I continue to have reservations about this proposed merger's impact on competition in the local telephone service market," Vacco said.

His concerns focused on how the merger could reinforce the monopoly position NYNEX holds in local New York local telephone service markets, in a period when regulators are aiming at prying open these markets to wider competition.
Vacco said he planned to investigate the antitrust implications of the merger.
"I will review the PSC's plan further to determine the impact this merger will have on competition and to ensure that consumers are protected from an anti-competitive marketplace," he said.
